findings.reason: it adds `reckon/crew/promotion_scope.py` (and the outcome-write sites) to the declared write paths, adds a case and a control for a comment written through the promotion writer, and forces the plan to settle whether that writer refuses the comment or the landing, so leaving it out sends the node down a path that measures the wrong callers.
findings.text: s3 asserts the store refusal is added "at every site that writes a comment or followup body" and lists four; the crew promotion writer (`reckon/crew/promotion_scope.py:1458-1471`) builds `{"id","who","when","body"}` and calls `_store.write_plan(..., {**state, "comments": comments}, ...)` directly, bypassing `apply_ops` and therefore the `comments` branch of `_apply_append` — and that is the producer of the very comments §1 cites: the phrases "Three follow-ons carry to §4", "Two follow-ons go to §6" and "its test-pin follow-ons go to §14" sit in `<div class="r-comment-body">` on `docs/plans/shared-coil-supply-model.html` (ids `c-close-s2`, `c-run-…`) written with `who="reckon-build"` by that path, so a node implementing s3 as written closes four sites while the one that wrote the evidence stays open, and the plan would not prevent its own motivating case recurring — additionally the `outcome` prose written by the `resolve` op (`_store.py:3849-3851`) and by `close` onto every open followup (`_store.py:4155-4160`) is authored followup prose outside the four sites and outside the audit's only guarded type
